mr_title: perf(memory): install derived internals on a per-constructor prototype
mr_description:
Moves lazily-derived `_zod` internals (`values`, `pattern`, `optin`, `optout`, `propValues`) onto a per-constructor prototype instead of installing an accessor on every instance.

Wrapper schemas shrink the most: `.nullable()`/`.readonly()` 2.4 KB to 665 B, `.optional()` 1.9 KB to 694 B. Construction of `.optional()` is ~1.96x faster; parse is unchanged. Costs +77 B classic and +13 B mini gzipped.

expected_issues.title: Derived constructors cannot override lazily installed internals
expected_issues.description:
defineLazyInternal() skips installation when the key already exists on the shared _zod prototype, so a derived schema constructor can no longer override a lazily-derived internal installed by its base constructor (e.g. exactOptional keeps the base 'optional' values).

Previously each constructor's init installed its own per-instance lazy accessor, and later (more derived) initialisers overwrote earlier ones. Now all traits of an instance share the prototype of the outermost constructor; base inits run first and install `values`/`optin`/... there, and the derived init's install is ignored by `key in proto`. Derived semantics are lost (z.exactOptional(...) reports `undefined` among its values). The accessor also memoizes `undefined` results produced while breaking recursion cycles.
